evals.prompt: A user asks to 'add retries to the payment callback' without specifying retry counts, backoff, failure thresholds, or what happens to the order state on final failure. The request names a concrete feature but lacks acceptance criteria. You judge the request vague and classify it as a grill intent. Clarify the expected behavior without designing the implementation yet.
evals.expected_output: A compact requirements record that identifies the unresolved behavior, asks only decision-changing questions (one at a time, with a recommended answer), and defines observable acceptance criteria.

evals.prompt: Two teams use the term workspace differently in the same codebase. The requirements capability has been activated via a grill intent to resolve the vocabulary and acceptance boundary before the migration proceeds.
evals.expected_output: A terminology decision with explicit in-scope and out-of-scope meanings, remaining unknowns, and testable acceptance conditions.

evals.prompt: The requirements capability has been activated for a vague request. After three rounds of answers the acceptance criteria are still partially unresolved. Clarify how to converge without asking more questions.
evals.expected_output: Record the unresolved items as assumptions (assumptions-recorded), keep the confirmed acceptance criteria and first slice, and unlock implementation without inventing user decisions or starting a second plan.
